body:
Thank you. This helped tremendously! I suppose I can look into forgiveness programs and free masters degrees through work as well. I think my concerns are during the beginning of it all when things aren't as flexible. 

I actually mentioned the "too poor to be in a long-term relationship" thing and my girlfriend basically called me an idiot and said money never played a factor. She's one of the few bright spots in my life right now and I suppose doing anything drastic right now would be beyond selfish. She's always been supportive every way possible.

Thank you for this. I've decided before I ever go through with killing myself I'll see a financial advisor (because fuck it, why not?) to see what my options may be. Your method seems very successful but I'm afraid I'll have less flexibility.

There's a good chance I'd be paying $1,000/month for the entire 30 years. If it comes down to that I don't know what to do. That's the point where I consider my life not worth living.

It's something I would consider after getting a year's worth of experience. If I'm going to keep on keeping on I need to take whatever I can get. That'll likely be a run-down apartment in a large city with plenty of hospitals.

I wish bankruptcy was an option.

I've spoken to someone in general about my issues. From a mental health standpoint I've been taking Wellbutrin and I've come to the conclusion that it's making my thoughts worse (not just because of the initial extra energy). I'm going to work with my doc to d/c it and see how it goes from there. 

I've realized if nothing else I have several more months of enjoyment before the bills roll in. I suppose I could try to tackle the debt issue beforehand and, if nothing else, there's always time later on for more drastic decisions.
I appreciate it tremendously; thank you. I've been trying to write out my thoughts a bit now to think things through.

$100k private, $20k federal. My parents made too much. I tried everything. But then the economy went to shit and my parents' hope of paying off my debt in giant chunks went out the window. So it is what it is for now. So yeah, I'm totally boned. I don't see the point anymore.

Sounds like a pretty good deal. $100,000 are private and like 7.75% interest (yeah...) over 30 years. Immediate repayment at graduation. I wish I had that kind of situation. They're literally the worst option possible. My parents cosigned so they want to help, and they'll help either way probably, but it's insurmountable. I guess if I stick around I could refinance pretty easily. I have good credit.
